newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba leaves discount, Lombard rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Buba leaves discount, Lombard rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its policy-making council had decided to leave the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.

The German discount rate was kept steady at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also left unchanged at three percent.
Economists had generally agreed that a cut in the bank's leading interest rates was extremely unlikely.
In a Reuter poll conducted this week, all 10 economists polled said they expected the discount and Lombard rates to remain unchanged.

Although soft October industrial output data fanned some speculation the Bundesbank might be tempted to nudge rates still lower in a bid to prop up economic growth, the Bundesbank reiterated recently that it sees no need to adjust rates now.

There had been some speculation in advance of the meeting that the central bank could decide to free private repo transactions from minimum reserve requirements at the meeting, but no statement has not been about that issue yet.
The Bundesbank said its council meeting was continuing.
